reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data through 2026-11-23: SPX closed 7,237.17, up 4.73% on the day but still 7.74% below its 120-day high, 4.99% below its 50-day and 1.54% below its 200-day; SMH $460.18 (+15.03%) and NVDA $165.05 (+31.48%) both remain BELOW Zone 2 after the bounce; VIX rolled over to 26.62 from a 35.89 five-day high and HY OAS 3.76 is calm; mechanical tally 3 of 4 with zone occupancy unconfirmed. This is day one of the first bounce after Friday's regime break — unconfirmed.
reaction.invalidation: A full give-back of the bounce day — SMH below $460.18 and NVDA below $165.05 on a daily close — with HY OAS above 4.00% voids the Watch stance and the ladder: that is a confirmed second leg, not a bounce. Conversely, a held weekly close above the failure zone (SPX 7,750-7,820) with VIX under 25 voids the correction read entirely.

reaction.trapRisk: Today's +31.48% NVDA and +15.03% SMH bounce came with SPX volume below its 20-day average (4.25B vs 5.64B), both names still below Zone 2, and SPX below both moving averages — a classic first-bounce shape led by the most beaten-down leveraged names (TQQQ +19.83%, CONL +13.96%). Do not chase it: entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict (SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH 580-600) or a Zone 2 reclaim. A bounce that fails at the failure zone is the trap, and the second low is where entries get sized.

strategyPosture: Watch. Research and stage the DATA_AHEAD names, but size nothing into the bounce itself.

themes.counterRead: A first bounce after a regime break and a confirmed bottom look identical on day one. The bounce came on below-average SPX volume and neither SMH nor NVDA reclaimed its buy zone, so the 'bottom is in' read is running ahead of the data. Positioning implication: no chasing; the verdict comes at the failure-zone retest (SPX 7,750-7,820, SMH 580-600) or a Zone 2 reclaim.
themes.dataAnchor: The bounce is real but unconfirmed at every level that matters. SPX closed 7,237.17, still 7.74% below its 120-day high of 7,844.52, 4.99% below its 50-day (7,617.6) and 1.54% below its 200-day (7,350.1), on volume of 4.25B versus a 20-day average of 5.64B. SMH closed $460.18 and NVDA $165.05 — both still BELOW Zone 2 ($470-505 / $175-185). Mechanical tally is 3 of 4, with zone occupancy the one unconfirmed signal.
themes.label: First bounce after Friday's regime break
themes.narrative: The market believes the bottom is in: SPX jumped 4.73% in a day, NVDA 31.48% and SMH 15.03%, with the most beaten-down names leading. The tape reads as a V-shaped rescue.
themes.watchFor: SMH closes inside $470-505 or NVDA inside $175-185 — Zone 2 reclaim confirms the bounce has legs.

themes.counterRead: Index-level calm masks real weakness concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight — the divergence itself is real and worth tracking, since credit conditions can flip. But with lending loose and credit contained, the data supports rotation over a confirmed broad rollover. Positioning implication: the damage is stock-specific, so selection matters more than index direction right now.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 averages 19.37% below 52-week highs versus SPY only 7.6% below — an 11.77-point divergence gap — while bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold). AAPL is the strongest Mag7 name at just 3.3% off its high; NVDA the weakest at 32.2%. The read state is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER, and credit agrees: HY OAS 3.76, calm, not cracking.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover: Mag7 divergence
themes.narrative: The market treats the selloff as a broad market break, with the Mag7 leading the decline and dragging the index with it.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4.00% or SLOOS turning toward stress — either would flip the read from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: The fundamentals-price gap is the setup the conviction engine is built for — but the gap alone is not an entry. These names are still in a falling tape with SPX below both moving averages, and AVGO reports earnings Dec 9 (AMC), so timing risk is live. Positioning implication: research and stage, do not size into the first bounce; promotion requires the tape to confirm.

Top conviction scores: DDOG 82 (tier A), AVGO 82 (tier A), ONTO 81 (tier A).
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI trade is dead — the narrative after the selloff is that AI capex was circular finance and the names deserve their derating.
themes.watchFor: AVGO earnings Dec 9 AMC, and any of DDOG/AVGO/ONTO reclaiming its 50-day while SPX holds above 7,237.

themes.counterRead: Credit calm is necessary but not sufficient: it says no forced selling regime yet, not that equities are cheap. The equity break happened without credit confirmation, which is exactly how a rotation reads — and also how the early stage of a credit break reads before spreads move. Positioning implication: credit is the tripwire, not the all-clear; the 4.00% line is the single most important number this week.
themes.dataAnchor: HY OAS is 3.76, flagged calm and not cracking, 24bp below the 4.00% stand-down line. The curve is positively sloped (2s10s +0.29, 2Y 4.63, 10Y 4.92), the real 10-year is 2.79, and the Fed funds rate is 3.88. Nothing in the rates or credit block confirms a funding break.
themes.label: Credit calm while equities broke
themes.narrative: The equity break reads as a credit event in the making — AI borrowers levered, lenders pulling back, a cascade coming.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS prints above 4.00% on a daily close — that voids the calm read and triggers stand-down.

themes.counterRead: A bounce led by the most beaten-down leveraged names is a short-covering shape, not a fundamentals shape. The holdings most exposed to it — CONL, BMNR, TQQQ — are the ones that fell furthest, and a failed bounce hits them hardest. Positioning implication: today's gains in these names are relief, not recovery; do not read them as thesis confirmation.
themes.dataAnchor: The bounce is concentrated in the most damaged names, not the strongest: CONL is down 58.85% in a month but up 13.96% today; BMNR down 35.61% in a month, up 11.12% today; TQQQ down 25.52% in a month, up 19.83% today; COIN down 33.52%, ASTS down 33.2%, SMR down 34.03%. Meanwhile BTC is down 20.36% in a month and was flat today (-0.15%), and ETH down 24.12% (-0.84% today) — the crypto bounce did not follow the equity bounce. These are Jun's own holdings: CONL, BMNR, DOGE (-24.52% in a month), TQQQ.
themes.label: Leveraged and crypto washout leads the bounce
themes.narrative: The bounce is broad and healthy — everything is recovering together, so the worst is over.
themes.watchFor: CONL or BMNR giving back today's entire gain on a down day — that marks the bounce as relief-only in the leveraged book.
